newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Only 5 pct NZers use tax cuts for retirement.
newsitem.headline: Only 5 pct NZers use tax cuts for retirement.

text.p: Only five percent of New Zealanders used the extra money from the first round of tax cuts to save for retirement, AMP said on Wednesday.
More direct incentives were needed to encourage people to save for their retirement, AMP said after surveying 1,000 people over 15.
However, as well as the five percent, 18 percent had used the cuts for some other form of saving including 10 percent saving for something "special".
The Reserve Bank had estimated that around 25 percent of the first round of tax cuts would be saved.
Forty percent of those surveyed said tax incentives would encourage them to save.

"While some people are clearly saving more for their retirement, the large majority of people are not -- and that has to be a worry for the whole economy," AMP New Zealand General Manager Rodney Cook said.
He said AMP believed the retirement savings advertising campaign and tax cuts on their own were not enough to get the majority of New Zealanders to save for their retirement.
In an earlier survey, 29 percent of those surveyed had said they would save the tax cuts for their retirement.
The latest survey said 12 percent would save the second round of tax cuts due next year for retirement while another 33 percent would save in some other form.
